head_commit.message:
feat: Doris continuous analytics [DHIS2-22183] (#24440)

* feat: add SqlBuilder capability flags for Doris continuous analytics

* feat: add primary-key-bearing AnalyticsTable constructor overloads

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: give DATA_VALUE/COMPLETENESS Doris analytics tables a unique key

* feat: emit DELETE...USING for Doris in JdbcAnalyticsTableManager.removeUpdatedData

* feat: emit DELETE...USING for Doris in JdbcCompletenessTableManager.removeUpdatedData

* feat: give EVENT Doris analytics tables a unique key and DELETE...USING support

* test: cover single-event Doris removeUpdatedData branch (review follow-up)

* feat: gate continuous-analytics delete/swap on supportsContinuousAnalytics

* test: cover swapTable() Doris insert-into-main branch and ClickHouse no-op negative case

* fix: Doris CREATE TABLE key-column ordering and swapTable() staging table catalog qualification

- DorisSqlBuilder.createTable() now reorders the rendered column list so primary
  key columns lead, since Doris requires key columns to be an ordered leading
  prefix of the schema. Aggregate and completeness analytics tables (where id
  is not already column 0) would otherwise fail CREATE TABLE.
- AbstractJdbcTableManager.swapTable()'s Doris insert-into-main branch now
  references the staging table via quote() instead of qualifyTable(), since the
  staging table is a native Doris table, not a federated one (same fix already
  applied to removeUpdatedData() in earlier commits).

* fix: composite unique key (id/event, year) for Doris Merge-on-Write partition requirement

Doris's UNIQUE KEY (Merge-on-Write) model requires the partition column to be
part of the key. Analytics tables are partitioned by year, so the key must be
composite: (id, year) for aggregate/completeness, (event, year) for event.
Confirmed working end-to-end against a real Doris 3.0.7 instance.

Also fixes DorisSqlBuilder.getOrderedColumns(), which built the leading
key-column block from natural column order rather than the primary key's
declared order. For a composite key, Doris requires the leading schema
columns to match the key clause's declared order exactly -- for the
aggregate/completeness tables, year appears before id in natural column
order (FIXED_COLS), which would have produced a mismatched schema.

removeUpdatedData() DELETE...USING SQL is unchanged in all three managers --
it matches on id/event alone and was confirmed to still correctly find and
delete rows regardless of partition.

* fix: narrow swapTable() Doris insert gate to isLatestUpdate(), not just isPartialUpdate()

skipMasterTable is computed from params.isPartialUpdate() (lastYears != null
|| isLatestUpdate()), not isLatestUpdate() alone, so the new Doris
insert-into-main branch was also firing for lastYears=1..N (a normal
bounded-years rebuild), not just lastYears=0 (the continuous/latest-partition
case this plan is scoped to). removeUpdatedData() never runs for
lastYears=N>0, so the branch was merging staging data into main without ever
purging rows deleted at source -- a real regression versus the pre-PR
no-op-drop-only behavior for that path.

Gate the insert branch on params.isLatestUpdate() as well, restoring the
exact pre-PR (safe, no-op) behavior for lastYears=N>0 on Doris while keeping
the insert working for lastYears=0.

* fix: bound the id key column's type on Doris (string not allowed as key column)

Real Doris CI (Sierra Leone e2e run) failed with errCode = 2, "String Type
should not be used in key column[id]" while creating the DATA_VALUE staging
table -- aborting the whole analytics table generation job, including
everything after DATA_VALUE in iteration order.

The synthetic id column (concat(...) of several dimension UIDs) was defined
as DataType.TEXT, which DorisSqlBuilder maps to the unbounded "string" type.
Doris rejects unbounded string/text as a key column on any key model.
event/dx don't have this problem -- they're already CHARACTER_11 (bounded
char(11)).

Give id a bounded VARCHAR_255 (Doris: varchar(1020)) type specifically when
sqlBuilder.requiresUniqueKeyAnalyticsTables() is true (Doris only), leaving
Postgres/ClickHouse's TEXT unchanged, in both JdbcAnalyticsTableManager and
JdbcCompletenessTableManager.

* fix: DorisSqlBuilder.tableExists() checks wrong schema, breaking continuous-analytics history preservation

tableExists() filtered on t.table_schema = 'public', but native Doris
analytics tables live in whatever database the connection is on (e.g.
'dhis2'), not 'public' ('public' is only correct for the federated
Postgres catalog). This meant tableExists() always returned false for
real Doris tables, so swapTable()'s skipMasterTable was always false,
so every continuous (lastYears=0) run silently replaced the entire
main analytics table with just the latest-window data instead of
inserting into the existing table - destroying history.

Found via a live manual test against a real Doris instance: triggered
lastYears=0, and confirmed the main table's row count and partition
history matched exactly what a full replace (not a merge) would
produce. Fixed by using database() instead of the hardcoded schema
name, which correctly resolves to the connection's actual database.
Re-verified live after the fix: history preserved, create/update/delete
all correctly reflected, "skip master table: true" confirmed in logs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: remove redundant public modifier on JUnit 5 setUp() [SonarCloud]

JUnit 5 test lifecycle methods don't need public visibility; the rest
of the class already uses package-private.

* Address SQ issue

* fix: avoid federated join inside Doris removeUpdatedData() DELETE

The Doris branch of removeUpdatedData() joined a live federated
Postgres datavalue table against local dimension tables inside a
single DELETE ... USING statement. Live validation found this takes
40+ minutes (killed, incomplete) versus ~12 minutes for a full
analytics rebuild on the same instance, defeating the purpose of
continuous analytics.

Split into: a plain federated SELECT (the same join shape already
proven fast by populateTable) that materializes matching rows'
natural dx/co/ao/pe/ou column values into a small native staging
table, then a fully local DELETE against that staging table. No
change to the main table's schema, key, or the Postgres/ClickHouse
branch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: scope Doris continuous-analytics window to last continuous update [DHIS2-21920]

The "latest partition" window used by continuous analytics (lastYears=0)
was always anchored to the last full rebuild's timestamp, never the last
continuous run's, even though that timestamp is tracked and already used
correctly for the "is there anything new" check. On Doris this meant every
continuous run reprocessed everything changed since the last full rebuild
rather than just since the last continuous run, with cost growing
unboundedly between full rebuilds - confirmed live: a single-row mutation
triggered a ~3.5 minute run, matching a ~96,000-row mutation's cost.

Scoped the fix to sqlBuilder.requiresUniqueKeyAnalyticsTables() (true only
for Doris) rather than the shared code path, since Postgres's "latest"
partition is wholesale-replaced on every continuous run (not merged), so
narrowing its window would silently discard previously-captured
incremental data. Doris merges into the persistent main table with
natural-key deduplication, so a narrower window is safe there. Verified
zero behavior change for Postgres (existing tests, unchanged, still pass).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: use the real latest-partition date range instead of a fake one on declarative-partitioning engines

DefaultAnalyticsTableService.getTablePartitions() replaced the carefully
constructed "latest partition" (with its real date range) with a "fake"
partition (year=null, no dates) whenever the engine supports declarative
partitioning - a condition true for Doris (and ClickHouse). With year=null,
isLatestPartition() returns false, so getPartitionClause() silently drops
the "dv.lastupdated >= ..." lower bound from the populate query, leaving
only "< now" - matching nearly the entire historical table on every
continuous run regardless of how narrow the intended window was.

Confirmed live: a single-row mutation produced a populate step matching
~21M rows and taking the same ~2.5 minutes as a full-table sweep, while
the DELETE side (which fetches its partition through a different,
unaffected code path) correctly matched 1 row in under a second. Captured
via SHOW FULL PROCESSLIST on Doris - the literal WHERE clause had a
double space where "and dv.lastupdated >= '...'" should have been.

Fix is scoped to continuous/latest-update mode only (isLatestUpdate),
preserving the existing single-combined-partition optimization for
regular multi-year rebuilds on declarative-partitioning engines, where
removing it would cause each year's populate call to redundantly
reprocess every other year (no per-partition year filter is applied on
these engines, by design, since they route rows to physical partitions
natively). Zero behavior change for Postgres, whose
supportsDeclarativePartitioning() is false, making the new condition a
no-op there regardless of isLatestUpdate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: target the actual physical table when populating the latest partition on declarative-partitioning engines

The previous fix restored the real date range for the continuous/latest
partition on Doris, but that partition's name also carried a year suffix
("analytics_0_temp") from the standard partition-naming logic. On Doris,
CREATE only ever builds one physical table per AnalyticsTable (the
master's plain name, e.g. "analytics_temp") - per-partition physical
tables are deliberately not created for declarative-partitioning engines,
since Doris routes rows to partitions natively within that one table.

Confirmed live: the populate step failed with "Table [analytics_0_temp]
does not exist in database [analytics]" - a table CREATE never built.
Failed during staging (before any swap), so the live analytics table was
unaffected.

Added a constructor to AnalyticsTablePartition that carries a real
year/date range but always names itself after the master table (no
suffix), and use it specifically for the declarative-partitioning +
continuous-update case in getTablePartitions(). Postgres and Doris/
ClickHouse full-rebuild behavior are both unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: avoid federated join inside Doris EVENT removeUpdatedData() DELETE

Mirrors the DATA_VALUE fix (7c1177c50b): the single-table join shape used
for populating (proven-fast) is different from the multi-way join a
DELETE...USING statement builds against a live federated trackerevent/
singleevent table. Materialize matching events' natural key (event uid)
into a small native Doris staging table via a plain INSERT...SELECT, then
run a fully native DELETE against that staging table.

Live-validated against a real Doris test instance: purge+merge for both a
registration program and a single-event program completed in ~10s total,
update batches correctly retained, soft-deleted batches correctly purged.

* fix: reject continuous updates against non-unique-key or bounded-years Doris tables

Addresses two review comments from Luciano on #24440:

- A main table created before unique-key analytics tables were introduced
  stays on the duplicate-key model until a full rebuild recreates it, but
  removeUpdatedData()'s DELETE requires unique-key (Doris only supports
  DELETE on unique-key/MOW tables). Add AnalyticsTableManager.
  isReadyForContinuousUpdate(), checked before a continuous run is
  attempted: it queries SHOW CREATE TABLE and refuses to proceed if the
  existing main table isn't unique-key, instead of letting the DELETE fail
  and letting the update continue regardless (removeUpdatedData()'s stage
  uses FailurePolicy.SKIP_STAGE, so a failure there doesn't abort the job
  on its own). Also make the abort explicit if removeUpdatedData() fails
  for any other reason, rather than proceeding to swap.

- A bounded lastYears=1..N update against an existing main table on a
  continuous-analytics engine (Doris) previously discarded the rebuilt
  staging data silently, since removeUpdatedData() only runs for the
  latest-partition (lastYears=0) case and merging without it would leave
  stale/deleted rows behind. Fail loudly instead: only a full rebuild or
  lastYears=0 are supported once the main table exists on such an engine;
  bounded updates are tracked separately as follow-up work.

Postgres is unaffected (no declarative partitioning); ClickHouse is
unaffected (no continuous analytics support).

🤖 AI Assisted

* refactor: extract swapTable() publish decision into a resolver method

Addresses Luciano's readability comment on #24440 (gist:
f93f938afb471511281593203159edd2): swapTable() packed together several
independent decisions (full vs. partial vs. continuous update, whether
the main table exists, how the database manages partitions, and how to
publish: replace/reparent/merge) into nested conditionals.

Extract a TableUpdateAction enum (REPLACE_TABLE, REPLACE_PARTITIONS,
MERGE_ROWS) and a resolveUpdateAction() method that makes the decision
once, up front, then dispatches to three small named methods.

This also generalizes the two fail-loudly behaviors from the previous
commit from Doris-only to any declarative-partitioning engine without
continuous analytics support (currently ClickHouse): a continuous
(lastYears=0) or bounded (lastYears=1..N) update against an existing
main table on such an engine now throws instead of silently discarding
the rebuilt staging data, since there is no purge step available to
make either publish safe.

🤖 AI Assisted

* fix: keep bounded lastYears updates working on Doris

A bounded lastYears=N update against an existing Doris main table threw an
IllegalStateException. Before this PR the same update gave correct results by
replacing the whole table, so throwing broke something that worked, including
scheduled analytics jobs that use "last years".

On declarative-partitioning engines the populate step does not filter by year,
so the staging table holds every year and replacing the main table is correct.
Return REPLACE_TABLE for this case on engines that support continuous analytics
(Doris) and log a warning that the whole table was rebuilt. ClickHouse, where
this path has not been verified, still throws.

🤖 AI Assisted

* fix: show continuous update readiness failure in the analytics job log

When a Doris analytics table was created before continuous updates were
supported, the continuous update for that table type was skipped with an ERROR
in the server log only. The job log showed the readiness check at INFO level
and the job ended as updated, so administrators had no sign in the job output
of why continuous updates were not being applied.

Report the readiness check as a failed stage with SKIP_STAGE, so the reason and
the required full rebuild appear as an ERROR in the job log while the other
table types are still updated.

🤖 AI Assisted

* fix: keep continuous and bounded analytics updates working on ClickHouse

On ClickHouse a continuous (lastYears=0) update threw an IllegalStateException
at the swap step, failing the whole analytics job. Before this PR the same
update gave correct results by repopulating and replacing the whole table.
The latest-update partition change in getTablePartitions() also applied to
ClickHouse, narrowing the staging table to changed rows only, so simply
replacing the main table would have lost data.

Only use the narrowed latest-update partition on engines that support
continuous analytics (Doris), so the staging table holds all data on
ClickHouse, and replace the whole main table instead of throwing for a
continuous update on engines without continuous support and for a bounded
lastYears update on any declarative-partitioning engine. Both log a warning
that the whole table was rebuilt.

🤖 AI Assisted

* docs: clarify event staging-keys delete matches on event across years

PRIMARY_KEY is (event, year), not event alone; year is only part of it
because Doris requires the partition column in a unique key. Spell out
that the staging table carries just event and the delete therefore
matches across all years, so an event moved to another year is still
removed.

🤖 AI Assisted

* fix: keep Doris continuous updates from skipping changes after an aborted run

When a continuous analytics update aborted for a table type (the
continuous update readiness check or removeUpdatedData() failed), the
type was still stamped as successfully updated, and on Doris the next
run's window started after the changes the aborted run never published.

AnalyticsTableService.create() now returns whether the update completed;
only completed types get their per-type last successful update
settings. On engines with a unique key on analytics tables (Doris), the
continuous update window now starts at the per-type settings rather than
the shared ones, which also advance when a type was skipped or aborted.
This is the read path switch deferred from DHIS2-21992 (#24899), for
Doris; Postgres still uses the shared settings.

create() returns true when there is no source data or nothing to
update, and false when the job was cancelled.

Co-authored-by: Luciano Fiandesio <luciano@dhis2.org>

🤖 AI Assisted

* fix: don't abort continuous updates for programs without an event table

A program created after the last full rebuild has no event analytics
table yet. removeUpdatedData() ran its delete against that missing
table, which failed, and the guard against swapping after a failed
delete then skipped the swap for every program of the table type. The
deletes already committed for the other programs were not followed by
their swap, so their updated events disappeared from analytics, and
every following continuous update failed the same way until a full
rebuild. Affects Postgres and Doris.

- Only remove updated data from tables whose main table exists; a new
  table has no stale rows and becomes the main table when swapped.
- Give a program without a main table all of its data rather than the
  continuous update window, so its new main table is complete.

Reported by Luciano Fiandesio.

🤖 AI Assisted

* refactor: extract continuous update preparation from analytics table create

* fix: Check Doris continuous update readiness before staging, publish per table [DHIS2-22183]

Review feedback:
- Check continuous update readiness right after the tables are known, before any staging
  work. A table type that is not ready no longer populates its staging tables in full on
  every scheduled run only to throw them away.
- On unique-key databases (Doris), remove updated data per table. A table whose delete
  fails keeps its staged data unpublished, the other tables are published, and the update
  is reported as incomplete so the window is not advanced and the next run covers it again
  (merging a window again is idempotent). Before, one failed table aborted the swap for all
  tables after rows had already been deleted from the others.
- Other databases (Postgres) swap the tables in after the delete whatever its outcome,
  unchanged from master.
- Limit the full-history window for programs without a main table to unique-key databases.
  On Postgres the latest partition is replaced with the same window on every run, so the
  epoch window made a new program's older events appear and then vanish; it also no longer
  queries tableExists per program there.
- Tests: drop class-wide lenient strictness for lenient() on the shared stubs that need it,
  and use assertFalse instead of assertTrue(!...).

🤖 AI Assisted
